themes_detail.label: Noise complaints surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a 2.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (a 118% jump, z-score 3.36), with residential noise also elevated at 211 complaints 3 weeks ago (86% above baseline). This emerging pattern suggests either a new noise source or deteriorating neighborhood conditions worth urgent investigation.
evidence: 6 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs 2.8 weekly average (118% spike, z-score 3.36)
211 residential noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs 113.6 weekly average (86% spike, z-score 3.47)
1,718 vehicle noise complaints over 90 days—second-largest complaint category after parking
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden noise spike this week? Construction, events, or new commercial activity?
Map complaints by subneighborhood to identify a specific noise hotspot (e.g., near arterial roads or venues)

themes_detail.label: Fireworks enforcement breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints exploded to 32 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (12,700% spike, z-score 48.0), suggesting either major enforcement gaps or a sustained July 4th aftermath. This is the most statistically extreme spike in the dataset and warrants immediate investigation into NYPD response protocols.
evidence: 32 illegal fireworks complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly baseline (12,700% spike, z-score 48.0—highest spike in dataset)
Timing aligns with Independence Day period, suggesting either holiday surge or delayed enforcement response
Single spike event rather than sustained trend indicates potential one-time incident or event
reporting_angles: Why did fireworks complaints spike so dramatically? Was there a specific event or location?
How did NYPD/enforcement respond to 32 complaints in one week? Interview precinct leadership

themes_detail.label: Food establishment violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK versus a 2.0-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (250% increase, z-score 4.47), suggesting a cluster of health or safety violations worth tracing to specific restaurants or vendors.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints last week vs 2.0 weekly average (250% spike, z-score 4.47)
Type of violations not specified in data; requires cross-reference with DOH inspection records
Spike is recent and concentrated, suggesting cluster rather than systemic issue
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or food vendors triggered the 7 complaints last week? Are violations clustered geographically?
Cross-reference 311 complaints with NYC Department of Health inspection records to identify violations (rodents, temperature, sanitation, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Asbestos hazard cluster detected
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (2,300% increase, z-score 8.69), likely tied to recent building demolitions, renovations, or a contaminated structure. This poses immediate public health risk and warrants DEP/DOE investigation.
evidence: 6 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
17 full demolition permits filed in last 90 days; 388 alteration permits filed—potential asbestos exposure sources
Asbestos spikes often tied to construction; cross-reference with DOB demolition/alteration activity
reporting_angles: Which building(s) generated the 6 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago? Link to specific demolition or renovation projects
Was proper asbestos abatement followed before demolition/alteration? Interview DEP and DOB enforcement

themes_detail.label: Traffic complaints and pedestrian safety
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked to 77 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a 23.9-complaint weekly average (222% increase, z-score 4.0), combined with elevated noise and street-use issues. This cluster suggests deteriorating pedestrian/vehicle conditions, possibly tied to major road work or event disruptions.
evidence: 77 traffic complaints 3 weeks ago vs 23.9 weekly average (222% spike, z-score 4.0)
538 traffic signal condition complaints over 90 days—underlying infrastructure issues may explain spike
Multiple 311 spikes (noise, traffic) in same timeframe suggest shared root cause (construction, event, or enforcement gap)
reporting_angles: What caused the traffic spike 3 weeks ago? Was there a major construction project, event, or signal failure?
How many traffic signals in the district are in disrepair? Audit DOT maintenance records for 164th St and Union Turnpike
